column1: # Mega Man Battle Network Legacy Collection Vol. 2 on Android (keys in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Game profiles on Android")
# A GBA emulator collection (Battle Network 4 Red Sun / Blue Moon, 5 Team ProtoMan / Team Colonel, 6 Cybeast Gregar / Falzar) with the NoesisGUI launcher of Vol. 1 (010038E016264000),
# SDK 13.3.5, NVN, Wwise; subsdk1 is NintendoSDK_movie. Update v196608 (1.0.3).
# Tested 2026-11-12 on an AYN Odin 2 (QCS8550, Adreno 740, Android 13) with Mesa Turnip (--vulkan-driver), driven with DM_CTL: the intro movies, the title, the main menu,
# Battle Network 4 Red Sun started from it, its title and opening scene (dialogue), the in-game options overlay and Quit back to the main menu; no crash, no red log line.
# 60 fps without a cap to remove: the collection presents every frame (interval 1); BN4's opening p99 16.67 ms, 0 dropped frames in 300, footprint 1.4 GB.
# It needed nothing beyond Vol. 1's core fixes (sync_replay_fence: the replay skips the movie syncs the game frees when each intro movie ends, which crashed the next allocation;
# nvnDeviceGetWindowOriginMode), with which it ran on the first try.
# The adaptive frame rate is off (DM_ADAPTIVE_FPS=0), as in Vol. 1 (its android.tsv has the measurements): the launcher paces itself to the vsync inside its own frame, so
# the work the rate judges sits at the period, a hiccup stepped it down to 40, then 30 fps, it never climbed back, and the GBA games, run one frame per present, slowed with it.
# Checked 2026-11-14 at Vol. 2's title under 8 busy CPU loops for 20 s: held at 60 fps, 0-2 of 300 frames dropped (Vol. 1 under the same load stepped down and stayed at 30).
# Known gaps: the launcher builds shaders in memory that are in no game file, the same 13 keys as Vol. 1's. A shader is captured on the device the first time a draw needs it,
# and only a port with --install pulls the captures into the game folder's build folder, which keeps them: a port into a new folder (or after its build folder was deleted)
# shows black menu backgrounds until a run and one more port with --install; neither the device nor Turnip is the cause. Qualcomm's own Odin 2 driver crashed Vol. 1 in
# vkCmdBeginRenderPass and ran it at 30 fps with DM_VK_RP=0 (the game then runs at half speed): port with Turnip.
# Played afterwards on the same Odin 2: Battle Network 4, 5 and 6, with saving, loading, battles and the gallery; no problem found.
